chapter: Films, Las Vegas and the union
title: Recording nightly with Kay Starr for the Lamplighter
summary: He describes the nightly sessions with Barney Bigard, Zutty Singleton and others organized by a jazz-loving columnist.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Over the years I suppose I worked with Barney quite a bit. Many records dating back to The Lamp-Lighter, when Kay Starr first started. We did all of her original things. You've heard of the Lamp-Lighter.
What was his name? Ted Yertzer(?).
He was also a writer for one of the daily papers here.
Wasn't it the Times? I can't remember.
I think it was the Daily News.

And he was a real Jazz buff, or fan as they say now. But he loved us all. I remember Allan Reuss, Zutty Singleton and Barney Bigard and Barney Kessel. But we used to record almost every day. We'd all get through work
at night, and there was some place on Kowanga(?) Boulevard...I don't remember the name of it. But that's where we'd meet every night and record with Kay Starr and whoever else.
Every night. This man just loved music.

Oh, for weeks. Oh yeah, we made probably 50 or 75 sides at least with this one label. I don't know who has all the masters. He released quite a few of them, but I know there's a lot of them that never saw the light of day. So they're still around somewhere. That's when 78's were the big deal. They'll turn up somewhere.
